scope: Kebu Liguey (K066) acceptance case 6: meaningful integration. The single most concrete, safely-scoped slice recommended after investigation: connecting case 1's worker profile to case 4's review flow, rather than building a speculative Rooms-on-hire or Network-connection-on-hire flow with no written spec.

mappedBeforeAnyCode.blindReviewConfirmed: Before this slice, app/api/liguey/employers/[businessId]/listings/[listingId]/route.ts's GET selected only job_applications.{id, applicant_user_id, cover_note, status, decided_at, decided_by, created_at, updated_at} — no join to worker_profiles or worker_profile_evidence anywhere. Even a join would have returned nothing: worker_profiles/worker_profile_evidence (20261016180000) had only ever had an owner-only SELECT policy. A reviewing manager saw only free-text cover_note + status — genuinely blind review, confirmed not assumed.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.networkConnectionPrimitiveConfirmedAbsen: Network (K067) has no 1:1 connection/follow/contact-request concept at all — purely a public directory. personal_connections (used by app/api/library/shares/route.ts) is a separate, older, unrelated feature — and its own table migration is missing from the entire migration chain (grepped supabase/migrations/, migrations_archive/, and schema.sql; zero matches), the same undocumented schema-drift class flagged elsewhere in this queue. Building 'connect hired worker to employer via Network' would mean building on a primitive that both isn't Network's and may not even exist as a real table today — recorded as a new flagged finding, not fixed here (out of scope for this slice).
mappedBeforeAnyCode.roomsOnHireConfirmedRiskier: Rooms CAN structurally have a business creator add a single external user to room_members today (app/api/rooms/[id]/route.ts's 'member' action does not check the target user's relationship to the room's business), but there is no job-application trigger, no 'hired' semantics, and critically no revocation primitive tied to application status (no rooms DELETE policy; archiving is the only lever) — the opposite of what case 6 explicitly asks for ('preserving ... revocation'). Deliberately not built.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.librarySharingNotReusableAsIs: library_shares' primary key is (node_id, shared_with_user_id) — strictly one user, no business_id column or business-scoped policy anywhere. Sharing an applicant's evidence with a reviewing business would need a genuinely new grant shape, not a reuse of the existing per-user mechanism — confirming the chosen approach (extend worker_profiles/worker_profile_evidence's own RLS, not library_shares) is the simpler, more direct fix.

fix.migration: supabase/migrations/20261016200000_liguey_profile_visibility_for_reviewers.sql — extends worker_profiles and worker_profile_evidence's existing owner-only SELECT policies with one additional OR branch: a business's active members may read a worker's profile/evidence if that worker has a non-withdrawn application to one of that business's listings.
fix.noSecurityDefinerNeeded: Deliberately simpler than every other RLS fix this session: the EXISTS subqueries read job_applications and business_members, and a reviewing business member already has SELECT rights on both of those specific rows under their OWN existing RLS (job_applications' 'any active member reads' policy; business_members' always-visible self-row) — so this policy checks visibility directly, with no bypass helper, no new recursion surface, and no new privileged function to review.
fix.revocationIsLive: Visibility is a live EXISTS against job_applications.status != 'withdrawn', not a cached/snapshotted grant — withdrawing an application removes profile/evidence visibility on the very next read, verified with a dedicated test rather than assumed from the SQL alone.
fix.apiAndUi: app/api/liguey/employers/[businessId]/listings/[listingId]/route.ts's GET now also fetches each applicant's worker_profiles row and worker_profile_evidence (joined with library_nodes for titles) — no separate authorization check needed, since a withdrawn applicant's profile query simply returns nothing, matching the DB's own grant exactly. app/components/liguey/liguey-employer-panel.tsx now shows headline/skills/languages/portfolio-evidence titles alongside each application's cover note, with an honest 'hasn't filled out a worker profile yet' state when none exists, both newly covered by the i18n dictionary (case 7).

verifiedScenarios.realSqlPGliteTests: tests/liguey/profile-visibility-for-reviewers.local.test.ts — 7 real-SQL PGlite cases against the actual migration chain applied verbatim, gated on KEBU_LOCAL_PGLITE_ROOT, run explicitly: a business member cannot read a stranger's profile before any application exists; once the worker applies, any active business member (not only managers) can read it; a member of a genuinely unrelated business still cannot; withdrawing the application revokes visibility on the very next read; the worker always reads their own profile regardless; portfolio evidence follows the identical rule; a complete stranger with no business relationship at all can never read it via this mechanism. All 7 passed.
verifiedScenarios.mockedRouteTests: tests/liguey/employer-listing-detail-route.test.ts gained 2 new cases (profile/evidence included alongside applications; profile/evidence tables not queried at all when there are zero applications, avoiding needless queries) — all 8 cases in that file pass.
